abstracts.value: We study the role of momentum fractionation in the development of chaos on smooth 3-charge supergravity solutions of D1-D5 theory, specifically momentum-fractionated superstrata. We probe the chaos through the dynamics of null geodesics and waves. On fractionated backgrounds, both geodesics and waves show uniformly strong chaos (large chaotic sea and near-perfect agreement with the Berry random wave hypothesis). In contrast, geodesics and waves on single-mode (non-fractionated) superstrata are closer to separability (although still chaotic). We discuss a possibility that such dichotomy can be related to the expectation that monotone BPS states are less chaotic than fortuitous ones. Finally, we explain why our chaos probes are meaningful for microstate geometries even though they become trivial in the black hole limit.

titles.title: Random wave chaos on momentum-fractionated microstate geometries

abstracts.value: Precision measurements of nuclear $β$ decay offer a powerful route to tests of physics beyond the Standard Model, but interpreting measurements spectra and correlation observables requires control of subtle nuclear-structure effects. This chapter develops a framework for calculating higher-order corrections--small contributions that can become important at the precision sought in searches for new interactions. After motivating their role in $β$-decay observables (with radiative corrections treated in the accompanying chapter), we introduce the relevant kinematics and multipole expansion of the shape factor, identify the subleading contributions, and present the impulse-approximation multipole operators. We then describe the nuclear many-body methods used to obtain the required states and transition densities, and derive the corresponding operator matrix elements in the harmonic-oscillator basis. Taken together, these ingredients enable systematic calculations of nuclear shape factors beyond the long-wavelength approximation, including higher-order multipoles where needed. By helping distinguish Standard-Model recoil effects from possible signatures of new physics, this framework supports the interpretation of increasingly precise $β$-decay experiments.

titles.title: Higher-order corrections to beta decays and nuclear structure

abstracts.value: Spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) is conventionally understood through static vacuum selection in low-energy approximations. However, the nonperturbative dynamical pathways connecting symmetric configurations to asymmetric states remain an open question. In this paper, we propose an operator-theoretic framework that characterizes $Z_{2}$ symmetry breaking in scalar field theory through spectral branching. Specifically, we identify an effective invariant manifold of the nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation termed the "symmetric dual breather mode," whose phase-space geometry is traced using a $t$-dependent finite-dimensional representation. Our analysis demonstrates that static SSB represents merely a small-amplitude limit ($A \ll ϕ_{v1}$). As the amplitude increases into the heteroclinic regime ($A > ϕ_{v1}$), the field dynamically overflows the central barrier, yielding a vanishing time-averaged order parameter ($\langle ϕ\rangle = 0$) and driving a geometric curvature cancellation ($\langle V''(ϕ) \rangle_{t} \to 0$). Governed by a universal scaling function $\mathfrak{F}(y)$, the logarithmic period divergence near the heteroclinic boundary naturally generates sub-eV effective mass scales without fine-tuning bare parameters. Furthermore, this dynamic barrier overflow naturally favors Majorana-like self-conjugate states over Dirac-type states. Additionally, nonlinear phase interference along the heteroclinic channel induces asymmetric phase-space contraction, decoupling the right-handed mode and dynamically giving rise to the left-handed Weyl equation. These results bridge nonperturbative wave dynamics, topological mass suppression, chiral selection, and the dynamic origin of active neutrino masses.

titles.title: Symmetric Dual Breather Modes as a Dynamic Origin of Tiny Particle Masses

abstracts.value: In this paper we provide an introduction to some of the efficient features of the Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2) family of microconroller boards (RP2040 and RP2350). More exactly, we show how to use PIO (Programmable Input/Output) and DMA (Direct Memory Access) to program the RP2 boards for efficient DAC (Digital to Analog) and ADC (Analog to Digital) conversions. Using OP-AMPS (Operational Amplifiers) we also show how to build a minimal electronic frontend interface for signal input/output. Finally, we integrate all these components into a product, the O-SCOPE, which is a practical and easy to use oscilloscope and wave function generator. The RP2 component of the O-SCOPE is built using Micropython, while the user interface is developed using vanilla Javascript and it runs on the web browser of any computer, interacting with the RP2 board via the Web Serial API. The O-SCOPE web interface is hosted on GitHub Pages such that it is directly accessible everywhere using a web browser, such that no local installation is required. Also, the RP2 software component is freely distributed on GitHub using the UF2 (USB Flashing Format) mass storage file, and it can be installed by simply dragging the file on the RP2 boards. These features make the O-SCOPE easily accessible, transforming it into a very low cost and useful tool for laboratories everywhere in the world.

titles.title: O-SCOPE: a Raspberry Pi Pico oscilloscope

abstracts.value: Entanglement entropies of multipartite pure states satisfy linear inequalities; for stabilizer states, the backbone of quantum error correction, the achievable entropy vectors generate a convex cone. We show that, after a linear lift, the closure of this cone is exactly the self-dual slice of a classical object on one more element than there are parties: the closed cone generated by the rank functions of arrangements of subspaces over $\mathrm{GF}(d)$ for a prime local dimension $d$, and of subgroups of abelian groups of exponent dividing $d$ in general. This correspondence brings two features of rank inequalities into play. First, the purifier acts as an extra variable: already for five parties the stabilizer cone is strictly smaller than the quantum linear rank cone, with which earlier evidence suggested it might coincide; an explicit six-variable inequality witnesses the gap. Second, the characteristic of the field enters, so the cone depends on the local dimension. It does not for up to four parties. With enough parties, the cone of $\mathbb{Z}_d$ qudits is contained in that of $\mathbb{Z}_{d'}$ qudits if and only if $d$ divides $d'$, and already for six parties the logical zero state of Steane's code lies outside the stabilizer cone of every odd local dimension. For this last result we show that the seven-variable characteristic-dependent inequalities we checked all follow from Shannon inequalities on the self-dual slice, and instead transfer one of them through a family of subgroups derived from the Fano plane.

titles.title: Stabilizer entropy cones as self-dual slices of linear rank cones: a five-party gap and dependence on the local dimension

abstracts.value: We report the detection of a ∼19 GeV gamma-ray spectral excess (peak energy in observer frame) at ∼5.7σ significance (3 degrees of freedom, without correction for trials and the look-elsewhere effect) in the Fermi-LAT data of the blazar 4FGL J0136.5+3906, based on ∼17 yr of observations. The excess manifests as a distinct bump-like feature in the 100 MeV to 1 TeV spectrum, with a flux of ∼3.6 × 10$^{−10}$ ph cm$^{−2}$ s$^{−1}$. No similar feature is detected in nearby sources or background regions. The origin of this signal cannot be explained by standard blazar emission models and remains unknown. This Letter presents the observational finding without providing a definitive physical interpretation.

abstracts.value: We develop a polylogarithmic structure for Bragg diffraction based on a weighted multi-plane interference model. Within this kind of construction, the scattering amplitude is expressed as a polylogarithmic generating function. By introducing extra contributions with power-law and the usual exponential decay, it takes the form $F(q) = \textrm{Li}_m\left( e^{i qd - \epsilon }\right) $, where $\epsilon $ is a finite coherence length. In the infinite-coherence limit, Bragg enhancement is associated with the approach of the polylogarithmic argument to its boundary singular point $z=1$. This formulation provides a compact analytical framework for describing diffraction line shapes within a generalized correlation model in which peak positions, widths, and line shapes arise from a single analytic structure. Although we are able to recover the standard Bragg law for ideal crystals, the polylogarithm model captures deviations due to finite correlation length, disorder and non-uniform lattice coherence. We show that if Bragg peaks correspond to boundary singularities of the polylogarithm, a connection between diffraction theory and complex analysis arises. The proposed theoretical model may be particularly relevant for disordered or partially coherent materials, where conventional diffraction models often require additional phenomenological broadening assumptions.[graphic not available: see fulltext] ,[graphic not available: see fulltext]

titles.title: Polylogarithmic structure of Bragg diffraction in finite-coherence lattices

abstracts.value: Distributed quantum computing distributes workloads that exceed a single processor's capacity across resource-constrained components. Circuit cutting enables this decomposition, but its effectiveness depends on partition choice. We present SACE, a Simulation-Aware Circuit Partitioning framework with Entanglement-Capability-Aware Screening. EP-Cost screens partitions using a parameter-dependent entanglement-capability proxy and native implementation cost. Under reconstruction constraints, finite-bond refinement selects the candidate that minimizes the worst-subcircuit discrepancy between normalized MPS simulations at bond dimensions $χ$ and $2χ$. Across 14 exhaustively enumerated small-scale candidate spaces, EP-Cost-guided genetic algorithm selections attain co-optimal native quasiprobability decomposition (QPD) overhead, with a median within-circuit Spearman correlation of 0.9965 between EP-Cost and QPD overhead. At matched cut counts, EP-Cost reduces QPD overhead by $25.20\times$ and $16.89\times$ for 8- and 9-qubit QFT circuits, respectively, and improves sampled reconstruction. On 12-qubit approximate QFT, deterministic reconstruction reduces Pauli-observable mean absolute error in all six low-bond conditions and total-variation distance in five. With five cuts and 7,776 QPD terms, SACE is best on all four reconstruction metrics in four of six conditions. At 24 qubits, SACE improves exact-local QFT accuracy in all 30 instance-bond-dimension conditions against each EP-Cost-only, Kernighan-Lin, and spectral baseline. The 50-qubit QFT comparisons remain favorable as reference convergence improves. Weighted QAOA circuits provide complementary, more bond-sensitive evidence. Refinement benefits persist across three search methods; larger candidate panels improve the optimized proxy without guaranteeing lower exact-local error.

titles.title: Entanglement-Capability-Aware Finite-Bond Circuit Cutting for Distributed Quantum Computing

abstracts.value: Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation is indispensable for modeling beam dynamics in particle accelerators, but its computational cost limits many-query workflows, such as configuration exploration, virtual diagnostics, and controller design. We introduce GLOBE, a physics-constrained Generative Latent Operator for Beam Evolution, modeling the nonlinear, control-dependent, multiscale evolution of 3D beam--field dynamics covering $10^7$ spatial cells. GLOBE compresses beam--field states into a compact latent space and factors their evolution into two components. A control-conditioned neural operator learns the dominant dynamics, while an amplitude-normalized generative model captures the residual distribution, recovering fine-scale structures and conditional variations. GLOBE enforces field constraints by regime-specific, parameter-free operators: a Poisson solve reconstructs the electric field in the electrostatic regime, and a spectral projection imposes Gauss's law and a divergence-free magnetic field in the electromagnetic regime. On two high-resolution 3D particle-accelerator benchmarks, bunched-beam transport and plasma-wakefield acceleration, GLOBE lowers relative-$L_2$ error by 9% and 13%, low-frequency spectral error by 69% and 51%, and mid-frequency spectral error by 54% and 20% relative to the strongest baseline (DPOT), satisfies field constraints, and reduces hours of PIC simulation to a minute per rollout.

titles.title: Learn the Dynamics, Enforce the Physics: Generative Latent Operators for High-Dimensional Beam Evolution

abstracts.value: Cancer detection using AI methods and image databases faces several challenges, including limited and imbalanced image datasets, long algorithm training times, and high-complexity feature generation. In particular, many cancer image datasets contain very few malignant examples compared to benign ones, limiting the amount of minority-class data available for training. Although classical AI and especially deep learning methods have had some success in providing cancer diagnostics, Quantum Machine Learning (QML) methods may offer advantages through high-dimensional feature representations, generative data augmentation, and the exploitation of feature correlations through quantum properties such as entanglement. In this paper, we propose using a generative QML method on the compressed breast ultrasound image dataset (BUSI) to generate synthetic images and hence augmented datasets for classifier training. In particular, we train a convolutional neural network with real, synthetic, and a combination of real and synthetic images. We test the algorithm on real images and provide comparative results for all three training cases. Our results show that the classifier trained entirely on synthetic images achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.802 (80.2%), compared with 0.760 (76.0%) for the real-data baseline.

titles.title: Generative Quantum Machine Learning Methods for Cancer Detection using Augmented Datasets

abstracts.value: We consider spin-coupled Grover walks on hypercubes within the framework of quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN). We identify parity-dependent harmonic subspaces generated by the central Hamming layers: in even dimension they give a fixed-point subspace, whereas in odd dimension the walk reduces on the harmonic subspace to an explicit eight-dimensional reduced dynamics. Using symmetric-group representation theory, we characterize the corresponding isotypic structure and determine the reduced spectrum. The harmonic reduction also yields explicit long-time probability behavior and shows that the resulting states may occupy an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the hypercube while still spanning its full Hamming diameter.

abstracts.value: We give an explicit treatment of the third tensor power of the Clifford representation on $n$ qutrits, for $n\geq2$. This representation has five pairwise inequivalent irreducible constituents, with multiplicities $1,1,1,1,2$. The decomposition reduces the Clifford twirl of a tensor cube to four real parameters. Two of them are spectral moments of the input. The other two are cubic invariants expressed as sums of cubes of the Weyl characteristic function and the discrete Wigner function. On trace-one Hermitian matrices, the invariant polynomials of degree at most three are spanned by the constant function and four algebraically independent functions. These functions do not separate Clifford orbits. For pure inputs a single parameter suffices. We recover its range and the characterization of its maximum by stabilizer states. We bound the stabilizer fidelity, determine full separability across the three copies in the symmetric family, and recover the criterion for a complex projective $3$-design. We classify the jointly invariant quantum Boolean functions. For stabilizer testing and for testing unknown observables we give explicit bounds on copies and queries. We also give character formulas for the finite projective Clifford groups and record the complete character table for two qutrits.

titles.title: Clifford Invariants and Three-Copy Quantum Tests

abstracts.value: We construct a chiral algebra $U$ of central charge eight inside the lattice vertex operator algebra $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$. abstracts.value: Free classical communication can yield an unbounded single-shot saving in quantum compression, even though it leaves the asymptotic rate of an i.i.d. source unchanged. At every fixed error in $(0,1)$, we exhibit sources whose unassisted compression cost is arbitrarily large, yet a single qubit suffices with classical communication and no preshared entanglement. We establish this separation by determining the exact optimal source fidelity for compression through an $m$-dimensional noiseless quantum channel, with and without free classical communication, while preserving correlations with an inaccessible reference. Without classical assistance, the optimal fidelity is exactly the Ky Fan norm $\|ρ\|_{(m)}$, the sum of the $m$ largest eigenvalues of the source state. With classical assistance, we obtain an explicit spectral threshold formula and a protocol attaining it. Classical communication strictly improves fidelity whenever $m$ is smaller than the source rank. The corresponding compression costs are two smoothed versions of the log-rank entropy, also called max-entropy: trace-distance smoothing under local operations and quadratic smoothing under LOCC. For i.i.d. copies of a fixed source with positive entropy variance, however, the two costs have identical first-, second-, and third-order asymptotic terms. For nonlattice spectra, we determine the constant-order advantage: classical communication saves $\log_2(e)-1$ bits per block asymptotically, and the ratio of assisted to unassisted minimum communication dimensions converges to $2/e$.

abstracts.value: Gauging fermion parity in a $(2+1)$-dimensional fermionic topological order requires lifting its symmetries to the resulting bosonic theory. We give a direct tensor-categorical proof that, for a slightly degenerate braided fusion category $\mathcal{C}$ and a fixed minimal nondegenerate extension ${\cal E}$, the restriction homomorphism $r\colon\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{E})\to \operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{C})$ on classes of complex-linear locality-respecting (LR) braided autoequivalences is surjective with central kernel $\mathbb{Z}/2$, generated by fermion attachment. Thus each symmetry class has exactly two LR lift classes, related by attaching the fermion to every vortex. We apply graded Morita theory to reduce the kernel to two module types on the vortex sector, corresponding to tensoring with the vacuum or the fermion. We then prove relative rigidity to show that each type determines a unique LR class, which are distinguished by fermionic self-braiding even when their actions on simple-object labels coincide. We prove surjectivity by extending graph algebras in $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{C}$ to Lagrangian algebras in $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{E}$. Our results require neither unitarity nor a ribbon structure. We illustrate the lifting ambiguity in the Laughlin state, the $SO(3)_3$ theory and the Ising topological order.

titles.title: Lifts of symmetries to minimal nondegenerate extensions are unique up to fermion attachment

abstracts.value: Area laws express the expectation that entanglement in gapped quantum ground states scales with a boundary rather than a volume. In one dimension this holds for every Rényi entropy, and the Rényi area-law conjecture asserts the same in higher dimensions for each fixed $0<α<1$. Here we disprove this conjecture in every spatial dimension two and higher. We construct finite-range Hamiltonians with fixed local dimension, bounded interaction strength, unique ground states and a uniform spectral gap, whose ground states exhibit volume-law Rényi entanglement while obeying a von Neumann area law and remaining connected to product states through uniformly gapped local paths. The mechanism is error-space complexity: locally identifiable components of arbitrarily small weight can encode states with high entanglement complexity. We also establish the worst-case rank-error trade-off for approximate ground-state projectors, a key tool in one-dimensional area-law proofs. At fixed gap, the optimal Schmidt rank at projection error $ε$ across a planar cut of cross-section $A$ scales as $\exp[\tildeΘ((A\logε^{-1})^{2/3})]$ when $\logε^{-1}\gtrsim A$. Thus $α=1$ is the sharp threshold for a universal Rényi area law within this adiabatically connected class.

titles.title: The Rényi area law conjecture is false below $α=1$ in high dimensions

abstracts.value: Quantum machine learning offers new approaches to multivariate event classification in high-energy physics, but its performance relative to optimized classical methods remains uncertain under limited training data and restricted quantum resources. We investigate the sample-size scalability and representation sensitivity of a quantum support vector machine and a variational quantum classifier for Higgs-boson signal--background discrimination using simulated events from the ATLAS Higgs Machine Learning Challenge. The models are trained on balanced subsets ranging from 250 to 4000 events and evaluated on held-out samples preserving the original class distribution. Principal component analysis (PCA) and autoencoder (AE) representations are examined to reduce the input dimensionality and quantum-resource requirements. Four optimized classical classifiers are used as benchmarks under a common preprocessing, validation, and evaluation protocol. We assess training-sample scalability in classical and quantum classifiers using a four-component PCA representation and examine representation sensitivity through a secondary matched-event comparison of four- and eight-component PCA representations. Within the evaluated Higgs-boson classification setting, the QSVM showed stronger performance than the VQC at larger training sample sizes, while remaining below the best-performing classical classifiers.

titles.title: Sample-Size Scalability and Representation Sensitivity of Quantum Machine Learning Models for Higgs Boson Event Classification

abstracts.value: Sensing time-varying signals is essential for precision measurement and for characterizing fluctuations in physical systems. In this work, we show that quantum entanglement provides an exponential advantage in the acquisition time required to learn the temporal statistics of a stationary classical signal. The task is to estimate the characteristic function of joint displacements on selected bosonic modes within a fixed-duration window, using continuous measurements of one signal realization. We present an entanglement-assisted scheme based on two-mode squeezed probes and local Bell measurements with protected idlers, and bound its acquisition time accounting for readout noise and correlations between signal windows. For a strictly stationary pulse family, it achieves polynomial acquisition time at inverse-polynomial accuracy with logarithmic squeezing and polynomial photon number. On the other hand, we prove that any local idler-free protocols require acquisition time exponential in the number of selected temporal modes per window. This lower bound holds for both sequentially prepared and arbitrarily temporally entangled probes, allowing non-Gaussian inputs and measurements and causal classical feedback, as long as each output is measured destructively within its time bin. These results establish an exponential quantum learning advantage for a single continuously monitored stationary signal, with the sensing cost measured by total acquisition time.

titles.title: Exponential Quantum Advantage in Stationary Signal Sensing

abstracts.value: We show that it is possible for three people to win the GHZ game with just the standard real valued misty state formalism, but each party will need to have two balls instead of one. That is, there will be six balls involved, rather than three. In fact, as a general rule, instead of using complex numbers in a quantum computer you can always add a qubit to "tag" complex numbers. But for proofs of non-locality, like the GHZ game, we cannot have a single universal tagging qubit, because all three parties would need access to it and therefore they could potentially transfer information via it. That's where we need to replace the one ball with three that each only need to be accessed locally.

abstracts.value: Can a holographic theory be reconstructed from its equation of state? We investigate this question using physics-informed neural networks in the bosonic-mass sector of the Pilch--Warner model. We first validate the PINN approach against an analytic solution encoding the leading high-temperature corrections to the conformal equation of state. We then reconstruct nonlinear black-brane geometries and the scalar potential using thermodynamics, ultraviolet asymptotics, Ward identities, and horizon regularity. Independent solutions of the bulk Einstein-scalar equations demonstrate that accurately reproducing thermodynamics with a trained PINN does not guarantee an accurate reconstruction of the scalar potential. High-precision knowledge of the high-temperature equation of state constrains nonlinear interactions in the bulk scalar potential. Fixing the cubic coupling to its exact PW value, motivated by this high-temperature extraction, reduces the maximum sampled error in the reconstructed scalar self-interactions by a factor of $\sim 15$ compared with constraining only the bulk scalar mass. Adding knowledge of the bulk viscosity of the gauge theory plasma further reduces this error by an additional factor of $\sim 13$, with independent forward solutions reproducing the bulk viscosity within $0.09\%$.

titles.title: PINNs for N=2* holography

abstracts.value: Most of the mass of the visible universe originates from the strong interaction. Quantitatively reproducing the origin of the nucleon mass is one of the important challenges in fundamental science. Since the next-generation Electron-Ion Collider has identified resolving this problem as one of its major goals, further theoretical studies are needed to develop approaches to investigating the origin experimentally. In this paper, we explore the possibility of evaluating the ``gluon condensate term'' which is particularly difficult to determine among the contributions to the nucleon mass, using high-energy scattering experiments. We first express the gluon condensate term in terms of experimentally accessible twist-4 lightcone matrix elements. We then derive, for the first time, analytic formulas for the cross section including all twist-4 contributions from pure quark, quark-gluon, and pure gluon matrix elements in $ep$ collisions, and show how these contributions can be related to the gluon condensate term.

titles.title: Seeking a possible approach to understanding the origin of the proton mass using twist-4 contributions in inclusive reactions

abstracts.value: Superradiance is a collective optical effect where emitters cooperatively radiate with a maximal intensity scaling proportional to the square of the number of emitters. Despite the superradiant cascade transitioning through highly entangled states, it has been shown that, for dynamics along the Dicke ladder, superradiance need not generate entanglement between the emitters. By contrast, we show how introducing incoherent local processes -- normally considered detrimental to both entanglement and superradiance -- can generate high levels of inter-emitter entanglement. We develop a general framework, using degenerate non-Hermitian perturbation theory, for the study of superradiant Liouvillian steady-state degeneracy breaking by these local operations from a few emitters up into the thermodynamic limit. From this, we are able to show that entanglement becomes ubiquitous in this regime and demonstrate its robustness against other forms of symmetric environmental noise. In the regime where pumping dominates, we find that population accumulates towards the maximally entangled minimal pseudo-spin states, corresponding to multi-emitter singlet states. This provides a deeper insight into many-body entanglement and the curious connection between local operations and entanglement generation.

titles.title: Entanglement generation from degeneracy breaking of superradiant Liouvillian steady states by local operations

abstracts.value: We present the concept of quadrature-detected zero-to-ultralow-field nuclear magnetic resonance (QD ZULF NMR). Two orthogonal sensors, atomic optically pumped magnetometers, are used to separately detect components of oscillating sample magnetization, which are then combined into a quadrature signal. This approach enables the distinction of positive and negative resonance frequencies with respect to the laboratory frame---such that absolute signs of gyromagnetic ratios can be determined. In addition, QD ZULF NMR reduces peak density and overlap compared to ZULF NMR with single-axis detection, while providing richer information about nuclear-spin dynamics. As an illustration, we present experimental $J$-spectra for thermally polarized [$^{13}$C]-formic acid and [$^{13}$C]-methanol, compounds commonly used in ZULF NMR which represent XA and XA$_3$ spin systems, respectively. A theoretical framework describing QD ZULF NMR signals is provided.

abstracts.value: Detecting weak magnetic fields at hertz frequencies is central to biomagnetism, geophysical sensing, and searches for new physics, yet it remains challenging because of technical systematics and environmental noise. Here, we realize a continuously operating molecular magnetic amplifier. Signal amplification by reversible exchange (SABRE) parahydrogen-based hyperpolarization maintains non-equilibrium spin order at zero field, turning scalar-coupled nuclear spins in liquid state molecules into an active, frequency-selective gain medium. Measurements of its complex magnetic susceptibility ($χ$) reveal an intrinsic response of $ | χ| \approx$ 10. By feeding the collectively generated magnetic field back to the spins below the threshold for self-sustained $J$-oscillation, we extend the effective spin coherence and cooperatively enhance the susceptibility up to $ | χ| \approx$ 80. Near threshold, this produces approximately fourfold amplification of a weak (20 pT) magnetic field at 3.37 Hz at the sensor location. These results establish hyperpolarized molecules as a tunable active magnetic medium for narrowband quantum sensing and precision measurement.

titles.title: Hyperpolarization-enabled cooperative molecular magnetic amplification

abstracts.value: Precise reconstruction of particle decay chains is essential for a broad range of analyses in particle physics experiments, particularly those targeting flavour physics and spectroscopy. We present a standalone, modular and extensible decay tree reconstruction framework designed to handle complicated topologies, accounting for tightly constrained particle decays and long-distance trajectory extrapolations through regions of intense and inhomogeneous magnetic field, as well as limited momentum resolution. Implemented in C++, the framework is optimised for configurability and performance. Developed primarily within CERN's LHCb experiment, its focus is on decay chains with vertices located several metres from the LHC proton-proton interaction point, where the dipole magnetic field is maximal and non-uniform. Even so, it remains flexible: it can accommodate these special cases as well as the approximations commonly used in standard decay tree fitting tools, and the geometries of general-purpose collider detectors. Benchmark studies using simulated data demonstrate significant improvements in reconstruction efficiency, invariant mass resolution, and vertex position resolution with respect to existing tools, opening new opportunities for precision measurements and searches involving highly displaced decays.

titles.title: Forward decay chain reconstruction with displaced vertices in intense magnetic fields

abstracts.value: Nuclear cosmochronology provides an independent method for determining the ages of astrophysical objects without relying on Galactic chemical evolution models. Long-lived radioactive actinides synthesized via the rapid neutron-capture process ($r$-process) particularly thorium and uranium serve as ideal chronometric nuclei. However, predicting the initial abundances of these nuclei and their subsequent long-term evolution remains a major source of uncertainty in nuclear cosmochronology. In this work, we investigate the impact of decay-chain feeding from long-lived progenitor nuclei on nuclear cosmochronology and estimate the corresponding age corrections. We develop a self-consistent radioactive decay network that includes all relevant decay pathways and couple it to $r$-process nucleosynthesis calculations. By tracking the long-term evolution of $r$-process nucleosynthesis based on neutron star merger trajectories, the dominant long-lived nuclei shaping the evolution of the chronometric elements Th and U are identified as $^{232}$Th, $^{235}$U, $^{236}$U, $^{238}$U, and $^{244}$Pu. It is found that delayed feeding substantially modifies the long-term evolution of actinides particularly for $^{232}$Th, which receives significant late-time contributions from heavier progenitor nuclei such as $^{244}$Pu and $^{236}$U. As a consequence, the U/Th and Th/X chronometers exhibit significant sensitivity to delayed feeding from the progenitor nuclei $^{244}$Pu and $^{236}$U, with age corrections reaching $\sim5$~Gyr. These results suggest that decay-chain feeding from long-lived progenitor nuclei plays a crucial role in nuclear cosmochronology and should be properly accounted for in age determinations based on actinide chronometers.

titles.title: Impact of Decay-Chain Feeding by Long-Lived Heavy Nuclei on Nuclear Cosmochronology

abstracts.value: Forward-folded X/$γ$-ray spectral fitting increasingly benefits from Bayesian workflows to better capture counting statistics, background uncertainties, and complex parameter degeneracies, while fully reproducible end-to-end implementations are still not always straightforward to deploy in routine analyses. We present ELISA (Efficient Library for Spectral Analysis), an open-source Python toolkit that streamlines the full spectral analysis loop for X/$γ$-ray astronomy: data loading, model construction, inference, and model validation and comparison. ELISA couples a JAX-accelerated forward model with a unified fitting interface, supporting both rapid optimization and modern Bayesian sampling. Built-in diagnostics make convergence checks and predictive assessment a standard part of the workflow, motivating principled model refinement when needed. Using a spectral fitting example of the Insight-HXMT Crab observation, we find substantial improvements in sampling efficiency compared with XSPEC's default MCMC implementation. abstracts.value: Generative AI can be a powerful tool for supporting the design and implementation of quantum applications, whereas the burden of checking whether generated circuits realize the intended computation increases. In this study, we regard this burden of human understanding, checking, and judgment as ``trust cost,'' and propose a development methodology that integrates AI and formal verification to reduce it. In the proposed development methodology, the implementation is divided into three components: a target mathematical specification, a quantum circuit, and a correspondence theorem and its proof that prove the agreement between the two. This division separates the specifications and theorem statements checked by humans from the theorem proofs entrusted to mechanical checking. As a concrete development example of this proposal, we describe an implementation for the time evolution of a stochastic particle system and its results.

abstracts.value: We derive Bondi four-momentum balance between past and future null infinity in the radiative phase space of the null-surface formulation (NSF). Weyl matching at spatial infinity, together with vanishing endpoint News, gives antipodal continuity of the Bondi mass aspect. Its translation projection is independent of the infrared shear term and transforms as a Lorentz four-vector. Bondi evolution relates the incoming and outgoing News fluxes to the timelike endpoint momenta; in the Dominguez--Kozameh--Ludvigsen radiative sector these momenta vanish and the fluxes are equal. On a common radiative Fock domain, unitary conjugation transports the flux observables. Adopting their classical balance as an additional quantum condition yields exclusive four-momentum conservation. We also calculate the outgoing energy expectation without imposing that condition. For an incoming energy eigenstate, the second-generator commutator vanishes diagonally, leaving a second-order coefficient determined by the cubic generator. Direct canonical contractions isolate the contribution connected to all four external legs. For the equal-energy center-of-mass preparation, axial rotational covariance forces the angularly integrated exchange coefficient to vanish under the finite helicity-projection prescription of Part~I. The connected energy defect therefore vanishes through second order. The full expectation (including spectators) and higher-order balance remain open.

abstracts.value: In this work, we study operator controllability of finite-dimensional closed quantum systems driven by a single coherent control. Two general Lie-algebraic results on controllability of such systems are proved. The first gives sufficient conditions under which controllability of the system is preserved when controlled energy-level shifts are added. The second gives a sufficient basis-element condition under which the dynamical Lie algebra contains $\mathfrak{su}(N)$ and the system is therefore operator controllable. These results, together with known controllability conditions, are applied to obtain a complete classification of operator controllability of all three-level quantum systems in terms of their free and interaction Hamiltonian matrix elements. This classification covers all combinations of energy-level and level-spacing degeneracies, two or three allowed transitions, as well as the presence or absence of controlled energy-level shifts, and gives necessary and sufficient conditions for operator controllability in each case.

abstracts.value: Trapped ion quantum computing based on the quantum charge coupled device (QCCD) architecture uses functional zoning and ion transport to enable high fidelity computation and all to all qubit connectivity. As trapped ion quantum processing units (QPU) scale, 90° X-junction turns account for an increasing fraction of total transport time. Frequent junction crossings, therefore, make transport speed and final phonon excitation direct determinants of quantum algorithm execution efficiency. However, complex electric fields in X-junctions complicate waveform design, making it difficult to achieve high speed and low final phonon excitation simultaneously. Here, we develop a waveform design method for low-phonon-excitation high-speed X-junction(LHX-T) transport. It integrates low barrier pseudopotential channel design using multiple radio frequency (Multi-RF), multidimensional shortcut to adiabaticity dynamics, and constrained DC voltage optimization over the entire transport sequence. This framework connects waveform design, control, and computational validation, with smooth multichannel waveforms computed rapidly through a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker(KKT) linear system. The resulting waveform transports a single $^{171}Yb^+$ ion through a 90° turn in $5μs$ at an average speed of 14.6 m/s. Over 50 consecutive round trips, the final equivalent coherent phonon number consistently stays below 0.001, with no noticeable accumulation over time. System level evaluations at the QCCD scale show that the median duration of a single execution cycle is reduced by about $30\%$ across various circuit types. The fraction of execution time spent on transport decreases from approximately $70\%$ to $55\%$. This approach offers a means of designing fast ion transport waveforms with low phonon excitation for scalable QCCD based QPUs and provides a technical basis for efficient execution of quantum algorithms.

titles.title: Fast continuous ion transport through X-junctions with low motional excitation for QCCD architectures

abstracts.value: GS 1843+00 (Ginga 1843+009) is a poorly studied Be/X-ray binary system that underwent a major X-ray outburst in 2026 February-May after nearly sixteen years of quiescence. We present an X-ray, optical, and radio study of GS 1843+00 during this outburst, focusing on the evolution of the neutron star emission geometry, Be-disk connection, and possible outflow activity. We analyse three NuSTAR observations obtained at different stages of the outburst, complemented by archival RXTE and Chandra data, optical spectroscopy and imaging with the Nordic Optical Telescope, and a MeerKAT radio observation. NuSTAR observations reveal coherent X-ray pulsations around 29.7 s with a spin-up rate of $(-5.1\pm0.1)\times10^{-8}$ s s$^{-1}$ during the outburst. The pulse profiles show strong evolution with energy and outburst phase, with distinct morphologies even at comparable luminosities. The pulsed fraction varies between 1 and 16% and exhibits a complex reversal in energy dependence above 7 keV, increasing with energy during the first two observations and decreasing during the third. The 3-79 keV broadband spectra are described by thermal Comptonization with a blackbody and an Fe K$α$ emission line, with no evidence for a cyclotron absorption feature. Phase-resolved spectroscopy reveals variations in the Comptonization and blackbody parameters, indicating changes in the accretion-column structure. Optical spectroscopy confirms the presence of a Be-circumstellar disk through H$α$ and Paschen-series emission lines. No radio counterpart is detected, with a $3σ$ upper limit of 36 $μ$Jy beam$^{-1}$ at 1.28 GHz. Weaker H$α$ emission compared with previous epochs indicates that the Be-circumstellar disk was in a different state during the current episode, while the radio non-detection suggests that any associated outflow activity was faint or below the detection limit.

titles.title: Reawakening of GS 1843+00: A Multiwavelength Study of its 2026 Giant X-ray Outburst

abstracts.value: Magnetar bursts are commonly attributed to magnetic energy release, yet the physically relevant dissipation unit has remained uncertain. Here we argue that this unit is not the burst as conventionally defined, but the short substructures within bursts, namely magnetar X-ray flares (MXFs). Using 789 MXFs from SGR~J1935+2154, we show that their waiting times separate into two components, interpreted as reflecting clustered intra-episode events and longer inter-episode intervals, that their proxy emission measure and temperature exhibit distinct rising and declining trends, and that their energy release scale (ERS) proxy distribution has a high-end slope in the same statistical regime as solar and stellar flares. Combined with the previously measured MXF duration slope, these results identify MXFs as a three-dimensional fractal-diffusive self-organized critical (FD-SOC) system with $β_{\rm diff}\simeq2$, implying reconnection avalanches that expand linearly through an active magnetosphere. We infer that magnetar active episodes are global unloading states assembled from many elementary flares. Magnetar X-ray flares are therefore the physically relevant units for magnetar outburst statistics and for connecting magnetar high-energy activity to other impulsive phenomena.

titles.title: Magnetar X-ray flares as elementary reconnection events in a self-organized critical magnetosphere

abstracts.value: This work explores the edge state conduction properties of twinned and spiraled, 2D Sb2Te3 topological insulator crystals. We show the structure supports spatially continuous edge states within two spiral and knotted edge conduction channels. The channels are connected through a topological defect. This geometry introduces boundary conditions into the 2D crystal that modifies the edge state dispersion. Using a combination of low loss Electron Energy Loss Spectroscopy, Magnetic Force Microscopy and traditional carrier transport measurements we identify a distinct excitation at 0.155 eV in the spiral that seems to be related to two isolated states within the gap. This state is localized to the crystal edges. The modification of edge state bands using manipulation of a systems quantum geometry may open new avenues for the use of 2D topological systems.

abstracts.value: Soon after Maxwell's celebrated synthesis of electrodynamics, the discovery of the electron raised fundamental questions about the nature and structure of elementary particles. The picture of a small, rigid, charged body of finite radius faced the difficulty of introducing non-electromagnetic forces or stresses to prevent the charge from dispersing, an assumption that was increasingly regarded as unsatisfactory. The alternative description in terms of a point charge was no more satisfactory, because its electromagnetic self-energy diverges. From the early twentieth century onward, several authors therefore explored modifications of Maxwell's theory, with nonlinear electrodynamics emerging as a particularly natural and radical possibility. In this paper, we revisit at the undergraduate level some of the nonlinear theories proposed in this context and explore their ability to address the classical self-energy problem of charged particles.

titles.title: On some nonlinear extensions to Maxwell's electrodynamics

abstracts.value: Linear-optical platforms provide a promising route to demonstrate quantum computational advantage, particularly through the boson sampling problem. While a boson sampling system should be large enough to show the quantum advantage, the size of the boson sampling problem is often restricted by experimental constraints. In particular, as a boson sampling system is scaled up, experimental constraints can limit its effective problem size to permit efficient classical simulation. In this paper, we investigate the theoretical scalability bounds for boson sampling systems under practical experimental conditions, including photon loss, mode mismatch, and input state error. We employ non-negativity conditions for phase-space quasiprobability distribution functions to analyze these effects. In addition, we introduce two device-level metrics, the boson sampling score which measures the usable capacity of a given device and the boson sampling volume which provides a common hardware-level benchmark for comparing different platforms and assessing their access to an advantage-relevant problem size regime. Our results provide fundamental insights into the performance of boson sampling systems under realistic experimental conditions and offer practical guidelines for scaling up boson sampling systems.

titles.title: Scalability and performance metrics for boson sampling devices

abstracts.value: We derive the secular Hamiltonian of a hierarchical triple from the 1PN ADM three-body Hamiltonian by a two-stage Lie-Hori-Deprit transformation carried out entirely in canonical variables, and use it to settle the relativistic cross terms left open in Paper I. A bookkeeping rule enumerates all contributions to each order in the 1PN parameter $δ$ and the hierarchy parameter $\varepsilon$. The 1PN monopole interaction reduces to a renormalization of the inner mass by its binding energy, and the order $δ\varepsilon^{3/2}$, at which Lim and Rodriguez (LR) found a libration term, is empty. The electric and magnetic 1PN $\times$ quadrupole cross terms agree exactly with the effective-field-theory result of Kuntz, Serra, and Trincherini; for the magnetic term this is the first independent derivation. We give the next-to-leading order 1PN $\times$ quadrupole term in closed form; it depends on the outer argument of pericenter $ω_2$. At quadrupole-squared order we obtain the complete secular Hamiltonian, which generates the secular equations of Will and of Conway and Will; its $2ω_2$ harmonic is a gauge term, removable even on the commensurability between the ZLK period and the nodal precession, by a generator given in closed form via Tremaine's fictitious time. The EIH and ADM descriptions coincide at 1PN order; the formulations differ only in the definition of the elements, for which we give the osculating-contact map. In secular integrations of LR's triples, the eccentricity enhancement with the octupole is controlled by the $ω_2$-dependent part of the next-to-leading order term and is two to three times that of Paper I, while LR's accelerated mergers remain absent.

abstracts.value: We investigate dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs) generated by a two-step linear quench with a finite waiting time at the equilibrium critical point. The waiting stage leads to the accumulation of a dynamical phase that depends on the waiting time and directly reflects the critical spectral structure. In the transverse Ising chain, this accumulated phase modifies the critical structure of DQPTs from a single-critical-mode (SCM) regime to a multiple-critical-mode (MCM) regime. We analytically and numerically determine the boundary between the two regimes. Along this boundary, the waiting time approaches a constant in the sudden-quench limit, whereas in the slow-quench limit it follows Kibble--Zurek (KZ) scaling with the quench time. In the SCM regime, the rate function exhibits a conventional linear singularity, $r(t)-r(t^{*})\propto |t-t^{*}|^α$, with the critical exponent $α=1$ near the critical time. At the SCM--MCM boundary, this exponent changes to $α=1/2$, leading to a divergent first derivative of the rate function. Additional discrete parameter lines with $α=1/2$ also appear within the MCM regime in the parameter plane spanned by the waiting and quench times. Our findings establish a direct connection between the accumulated dynamical phase and the critical structure of DQPTs, further supported by an extended Su--Schrieffer--Heeger (SSH) model.

titles.title: Exploring Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions via the Dynamical Phase Accumulated at an Equilibrium Critical Point

abstracts.value: We study electrically charged black branes in four-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory with Maxwell coupling $Z(ϕ)=e^{3ϕ/\sqrt7}$, whose potential has an AdS$_4$ fixed point only in the infrared. For nonzero hair parameter $α$ the scalar grows logarithmically at large radius and the geometry is not asymptotically AdS, so the holographic dictionary is a working assumption. With the scale-invariant multi-trace boundary condition of the neutral branes, giving conformal thermodynamics, we work to second order in the charge, obtaining the Maxwell field and susceptibility in closed form, plus the thermodynamics, condensate, incoherent conductivity and cumulant ratio $T^2χ_4/χ_2=6c(α)<0$ for all $α$ considered. Independent perturbative computations and first-law closed forms agree within $4\times10^{-6}$; nonlinear solutions reproduce second-order results to $1.2\times10^{-5}$ and $c$ to $6\times10^{-4}$. They are locally thermodynamically stable where constructed, and the pressure is analytic in $(μ_Q/T)^2$ near zero density. No regular extremal horizon exists at finite scalar value, and $ρ/s<\sqrt{21}/(2π)$ exactly. The extremal limit is an AdS$_2\times\mathbb R^2$ throat where the scalar grows as $\ln\ln(1/u)$ in the AdS$_2$ radial coordinate $u$; the bound is saturated there, and extremal values are approached as powers of $1/\ln(μ_Q/T)$. With a Dirichlet condition on the scalar source, the same solutions describe a non-conformal theory with scale $Λ$, whose charged branes exist only below $T_{\max}(μ_Q)$, which falls from $0.194Λ$ at zero density to zero at $μ_Q=0.506Λ$. This boundary is a diffusive instability where the charge susceptibility diverges at nonzero density, and the bulk viscosity violates Buchel's bound at all densities. Quasinormal modes with the normalizable large-radius condition reproduce its hydrodynamics.

abstracts.value: We investigate the gravitational waves generated by first-order phase transitions (PTs) in an expanding Universe. Using a scalar field-fluid coupled model, we perform three-dimensional lattice numerical simulations of slow first-order PTs with strong strength. We observe that the contribution from sound waves to the gravitational wave (GW) signal significantly dominates over that from bubble collisions. The sound wave spectra exhibit two peaks located at the mean bubble separation and the sound-shell width. Rotational modes are generated in the fluid during the bubble collisions, and their magnitude grows with the PT strength. The lifetime of the sound wave source increases with decreasing $α$: for weaker transitions the source can persist for longer than a Hubble time, while for stronger transitions it decays within a Hubble time. When the walls propagate as deflagrations, the GW spectral shape changes drastically, with steeper ultraviolet tails and a shorter-lived sound wave source. We also observe that the magnitude of the normalized GWs is roughly an order of magnitude smaller than obtained in the Minkowski spacetime simulations.

titles.title: Gravitational waves from strong first-order phase transitions in an expanding Universe

abstracts.value: We show that a quantum reservoir computer optimized with its quantum Fisher information (QFI) has a quantum advantage over a classical reservoir of equal readout cost, provided by a quantum-information advantage: optimizing the quantum parameters with the QFI metric. On Mackey-Glass forecasting, a driven Jaynes-Cummings reservoir with one to three atoms beats a tuned echo-state network at every size from 4 to 30 trained weights, by 25-69% in held-out error, and is ahead of 99.5% of 10,000 random networks. After grid and Bayesian searches saturate, the QFI-aware stage lowers the error by 29-51% at 12-30 weights, beyond equal-budget black-box search or classical-parameter gradients alone, and at 30 weights turns a loss into a win. We then derive a fundamental QFI bound on the first-order rate of change of the retrained loss and factorize the gap to this bound into five link efficiencies that identify the physical mechanism limiting optimization.

abstracts.value: Characteristic modes provide important information about the intrinsic properties and dynamical response of gravitational systems. In this work, we investigate characteristic modes of thick branes with a non-minimally coupled bulk scalar field. Two representative thick brane solutions are considered, corresponding to a single-kink scalar configuration and a deformed kink configuration with internal structure, respectively. By analyzing the tensor perturbation equations, we first examine the localization of the graviton zero mode in the two brane models. For both brane models, the graviton zero mode is localized on the brane. No pronounced resonant Kaluza--Klein (KK) modes are found for the single-kink brane at $ξ=1/7$. For the deformed brane, we investigate the resonant KK modes at $ξ=0.99$, finding that increasing the deformation parameter $k$ leads to more resonant modes and a longer-lived first resonance. We then calculate the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of both brane models independently in the frequency and time domains. The quasinormal frequencies (QNFs) obtained by the independent methods agree well for the low overtones. The masses and decay rates of the resonant KK modes agree closely with the real parts and the magnitudes of the imaginary parts of the corresponding QNFs, respectively.

abstracts.value: We consider the stability of light rings in four-dimensional circular stationary axisymmetric spacetimes. Using a Hamiltonian formalism for null geodesics and the Killing symmetries of the spacetime, we show that the transverse Hessian of the geodesic potential, which controls the light ring's stability, reduces there to a pure curvature expression. Its eigenvalues are $μ_{\pm} = Φ_{0 0} \pm \lvert Ψ_{0} \rvert$, where $Φ_{0 0}$ is a Ricci scalar and $Ψ_{0}$ a Weyl scalar of a complex null tetrad adapted to the light ring. Through the Sachs optical equations, these quantities are responsible for focussing and shear of a null geodesic congruence. Stability requires both eigenvalues to be positive, so a light ring is stable if and only if $Φ_{0 0} > \lvert Ψ_{0} \rvert$ there. Assuming the Einstein field equations with generic stress--energy tensor $T_{a b}$, we recast this as $4 πT_{a b} p^{a} p^{b} > \lvert Ψ_{0} \rvert$, where $p^{a}$ is the light ring's tangent vector: for stability, the focussing by matter must dominate the local tidal shear. The trace of the Hessian alone provides an inexpensive test of stability, requiring no knowledge of the Weyl curvature, since a light ring at which the strict null energy condition is violated cannot be stable. Applying the test to specific matter models, we recover known results for vacuum and electrovacuum, with and without a cosmological constant. We also demonstrate that stable light rings are forbidden for a minimally coupled real scalar field with any self-interaction potential, since such a field must be invariant under both isometries. We show that a complex scalar field escapes this obstruction whenever it carries harmonic dependence on the Killing coordinates.

titles.title: Stability conditions for light rings in circular stationary axisymmetric spacetimes

abstracts.value: We show that gravity can remove the linear magnetic instability of a holographic plasma with an $SU(2)$ global symmetry. The critical field diverges as the coupling $α= κ^2/\hat g^2$ approaches $α_\star = 2/3$, above which the normal phase has no linear charged instability at any field or temperature: we show this at zero temperature and establish it numerically at finite temperature. At zero temperature the field cancels from the mass of the lowest Landau level in the brane's AdS$_3 \times \mathbb{R}^2$ throat, and the instability is a violation of the throat's Breitenlohner-Freedman bound. The onset temperature vanishes at $α_\star$ with an essential singularity of Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless type. For two-derivative Einstein-Yang-Mills duals in $d = 4$, 5 and 6 dimensions the normal phase has a charged instability if and only if $C_J/C_T < 8/(d^2(d+1))$, one tenth in $d = 4$. abstracts.value: Quantum generative models face growing qubit requirements and concentrated loss landscapes when learning long time series. Here we introduce holographic quantum circuit sampling (HQCS), which combines mid-circuit measurements, qubit reuse and independently parameterized temporal blocks to generate trajectories with a fixed number of qubits. For Haar-random HQCS and a normalized exponential kernel, we prove inverse-polynomial bounds on maximum mean discrepancy loss variance, contrasting with exponential concentration in global Haar-random generators. For generic members of a family of nonstationary Markov processes, temporal parameterization reduces exact-generation gate counts from quadratic to linear in sequence length relative to a specified class of repeated shared-block generators. Simulations demonstrate learning of Gaussian autoregressive processes and historical Volatility Index (VIX) trajectories, with the latter achieving over tenfold lower maximum mean discrepancy than the tested classical benchmarks. These results establish a framework for quantum time-series generation with fixed qubit requirements and provable avoidance of exponential loss concentration as sequence length grows.

abstracts.value: Quantum science and engineering increasingly target the exploitation and control of large-scale dynamical systems. As system size grows, novel phenomena and quantum advantages emerge, but the resulting many-body dynamics become correspondingly harder to monitor and characterize. In particular, the underlying Hamiltonian often lacks symmetries, and the induced many-body dynamics quickly become hard to track. Focusing on one of the most important quantum features---entanglement---we demonstrate that, for a broad class of common Hamiltonian models, one can design effective witnesses that detect both the presence and structure of entanglement over relatively long evolution times. Inspired by stabilizer-based simulation, we track the evolution of generalized stabilizers of the underlying state and use them to construct linear entanglement witnesses. Through numerical experiments on Heisenberg-type Hamiltonians with up to twelve qubits, we show that the required number of measurement settings can be kept at a modest scale as the system size increases, and entanglement detection remains effective over evolution times that significantly exceed those accessible to naive approaches. The corresponding calculations can be carried out largely symbolically. Furthermore, unlike accurate state simulation, the stabilizer-based design of entanglement witnesses can be performed in a much more coarse-grained, digitized manner. We hope these results will stimulate further exploration of the quantum control of large systems.

titles.title: Entanglement detection in dynamical quantum systems

abstracts.value: A mixed leptogenesis source and its low-energy neutrino portal depend on the same heavy-particle amplitudes. We determine how this common origin restricts matching cancellations and the scalar population produced during reheating. For two Majorana mass levels, each containing a degenerate pair, the inclusive lepton-number-violating invariant fixes an allowed norm domain for the mixed dimension-five coefficient at specified threshold strengths. An aligned flavour texture makes the conventional source vanish as a matrix and gives equal coupling norms for the two massive neutrinos. A continuous family preserves the neutrino-mass fit while relating the source to unequal light coupling strengths. The matched couplings give benchmark vacuum lifetimes of $1.62\times10^{12}\,\mathrm{s}$ and $2.80\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{s}$, while reheating normalized to the baryon abundance determines the primary spectrum. In the massless Born approximation with dilute outgoing states, bath-produced scalars carry $4.81\times10^{-5}$ of the primary scalar energy but contribute $11.1$ times its variance. The positive production functional converts the matching constraint into a conditional variance bound. We derive the scalar-mass dependence of stimulated emission and the Hartree moment equation, keeping the scalar mass and quartic as renormalized matching inputs. These results link the leptogenesis source to light-neutrino decay and the finite-density quantities entering subsequent coupled transport.

titles.title: Mixed leptogenesis sources and low-energy neutrino portals

abstracts.value: An eV-scale sterile Majorana neutrino can suppress neutrinoless double-beta decay through destructive interference with the active-neutrino contribution, weakening the resulting constraints on sterile-neutrino parameters. We investigate how complementary beta-decay information restricts this cancellation in the 3+1 framework. Using updated oscillation parameters that include the first JUNO results, we determine the allowed sterile-neutrino mass and mixing regions for both normal and inverted ordering. We show that an upper limit on the effective beta-decay mass $m_β$ of the three light neutrinos strengthens the constraints from neutrinoless double-beta decay alone. The beta-decay bound restricts the light-neutrino masses and hence the cancellation between the active and sterile contributions to $m_{ββ}$. We derive analytic expressions for the resulting boundaries and use complex-plane geometry to explain the allowed values of the sterile Majorana phase $α_4$ for a finite $|m_{ββ}|$ limit. For the mixing considered, normal ordering allows a broad range of $α_4$ at small sterile masses, whereas inverted ordering favors values near $π$. The allowed phase range narrows as the sterile mass approaches its upper bound or the limit on $|m_{ββ}|$ becomes more stringent.

titles.title: Probing eV-scale sterile neutrinos with neutrinoless double-beta decay and beta decay

abstracts.value: We present cosmological constraints from 11 strongly lensed quasars with measured time delays (hereafter, the TDCOSMO-2026 sample). In addition to expanding the sample, we improve many aspects of our blind analysis with respect to our 2025 analysis. Among other improvements, spatially resolved kinematics are available for nine systems, including six with JWST-NIRSpec, compared to one in 2025; for three lens models, JWST-NIRCam images now replace HST; axisymmetric dynamical modeling is applied directly to the spatially resolved data, instead of an axisymmetric correction factor applied to spherical models; and the line-of-sight convergence is now based on the Euclid Flagship simulations instead of the Millennium Simulation. Our baseline and primary result is based on the TDCOSMO-2026 sample, in combination with a prior on $Ω_{\rm m}$ from the DES-Dovekie supernova sample. In the flat $Λ$ cold dark matter ($Λ$CDM) cosmology, we find $H_0=71.1^{+2.4}_{-2.3}$ km.s$^{-1}$.Mpc$^{-1}$, a 3.3% uncertainty that accounts for the mass-sheet degeneracy. The SLACS and SL2S samples are in excellent agreement with the TDCOSMO-2026 sample, improving the precision on $H_0$ in flat $Λ$CDM to 3.0%. Using the DESI-DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) likelihood instead of DES-Dovekie yields fully consistent results. We also present constraints in the open $Λ$CDM, $w$CDM, $w_0w_a$CDM, and $w_ϕ$CDM cosmologies; the TDCOSMO $H_0$ inference is robust and consistent across all of them. The combination of the TDCOSMO+SLACS+SL2S likelihood with those from DESI-DR2 and DES-Dovekie disfavors $w=-1$ at the $2.3$-$2.5σ$ level in all three dark energy extensions that we tested. We find, e.g., $w_0=-0.88^{+0.04}_{-0.05}$ in $w_ϕ$CDM and $w_0 = -0.85^{+0.07}_{-0.06}$ in $w_0w_a$CDM, while $w_a = -0.48^{+0.46}_{-0.44}$ remains consistent with zero.

titles.title: TDCOSMO 2026: A 3% measurement of the Hubble constant from strong lensing and stellar kinematics

abstracts.value: Self-force effects are essential for accurately describing the motion of small bodies in curved spacetime. The effective-source approach privides a promising route to higher-order self-force calculations. In this paper, we construct analytic electromagnetic effective source for geodesic motion in Schwarzschild spacetime. An angular completion and a tetrad decomposition express the vector-harmonic puncture modes as finite sums of scalar modes. We derive the coupling coefficients for both parity sectors and obtain the effective sources from the Maxwell mode equations. The point-particle delta contribution cancels, and representative eccentric-orbit results show finite mode sources near the particle. These expressions provide the source terms for future $1+1$-dimensional residual-field calculations.

titles.title: Analytic Electromagnetic Effective Source for Geodesic Orbit in Schwarzschild Spacetime

abstracts.value: Next-generation e+e-colliders have been proposed for the Super Tau Charm Facility covering center-of-mass energies sqrt(s) = 2-7 GeV, and for the Higgs Factories optimized for Z-pole physics and for HZ production. Luminosity can be determined by measuring forward Bhabha scattering. The QED cross-section calculation has reached a precision of better than 10^-3. Detecting radiative photons in Bhabha events provides a tool for validating higher-order corrections in theory. We propose the Forward Detector for detecting Bhabha scattering events at the STCF. The design uses high-resolution silicon detectors and finely segmented LYSO crystals to discriminate radiative photons from closely associated electrons. Bhabha scattering events are simulated with the BHLUMI and BHWIDE programs, and the detector is modeled using GEANT. Systematic uncertainties due to multiple scattering and bremsstrahlung in the beam pipe were evaluated. The potential for achieving precise measurements of radiative processes in Bhabha events is investigated.

titles.title: Detecting photons in radiative Bhabha interaction with Si-strip and LYSO crystals at future e+e- colliders

abstracts.value: Weak measurement has proven useful for metrology, for probing quantum paradoxes, and for the direct measurement of quantum states. Weak measurements of polarization qubits with temporal pointers provide a direct route to weak-value characterization, including in regimes where the pointer is only partially coherent. We derive a closed-form expression for the post-selected temporal shift that interpolates between the incoherent and coherent (ideal) weak-measurement limits through a single parameter $ν$, the pointer visibility. The expression is experimentally tested for a range of polarization states spanning three trajectories corresponding to rotations about the principal axes of the Poincaré sphere. Two of the trajectories provide parameter-free benchmarks, with the real part of the weak value following $\cos^2θ$ and $1/2$. In contrast, the weak value along the third trajectory is sensitive to incoherence and is well described by the single-parameter partial-coherence model, from which a reduced pointer visibility is obtained. Time shifts are extracted from the smoothed derivative of the pulse leading edge with internal calibration, reaching few-picosecond precision on 10 ns optical pulses using commercial components. The same apparatus also gives qualitative access to the imaginary quadrature through the frequency centroid, showing that temporal weak measurements remain accessible and quantitative in partially coherent pulsed systems.

titles.title: Partial-coherence weak measurement of polarization qubits with a temporal pointer: theory and experiment

abstracts.value: The energy densities of the quantised scalar and electromagnetic fields need not be positive, but their averages along timelike worldlines are constrained by Quantum Energy Inequalities (QEIs) that hold in flat and curved spacetimes for arbitrary Hadamard quantum field states. However the general QEI bound is not easy to compute in closed form. Here, we compute closed form expressions for the massless scalar and electromagnetic fields along stationary worldlines in Minkowski spacetime. These worldlines are solutions to the four-dimensional Frenet-Serret equations with constant curvature invariants and include inertial, uniformly linearly accelerated, and uniformly rotating worldlines as special cases. The QEI bound depends on a choice of tetrad along the worldline, and we compute it for any tetrad with constant angular velocity relative to the Frenet-Serret tetrad. Optimising over the angular velocity, we show that the tightest electromagnetic QEI bound occurs when the tetrad is invariant under Fermi-Walker tetrads. Surprisingly, the Fermi-Walker tetrad does not produce the tightest QEI bound for massless scalar fields, and we investigate the optimal bound both analytically and numerically. Our results and methodology significantly improve on those in [CJ Fewster & J Thompson, Class. Quantum Grav. 40 (2023) 175008], in which only Frenet-Serret tetrads were considered for massless scalar fields.

titles.title: Quantum Energy Inequalities with a twist: rotating frames along stationary worldlines

abstracts.value: We discuss the measurement of the Hubble constant ($H_0$) in flat $Λ$ cold dark matter cosmology based on the blind hierarchical analysis of 11 multiply-imaged quasars (hereafter the TDCOSMO-2026 sample) and described in greater detail in a companion paper. In addition to the time delays, we use lens models based on high-resolution imaging from the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), analyzed jointly with axisymmetric dynamical models based on JWST-NIRSpec, VLT-MUSE, and Keck-KCWI spectroscopy. Our primary result $H_0=71.1^{+2.4}_{-2.3}$ km.s$^{-1}$.Mpc$^{-1}$ is based on the TDCOSMO-2026 sample, in combination with $Ω_{\rm m}$ constraints from the DES-Dovekie supernova (SN) dataset. Our 3% precision accounts for the mass-sheet degeneracy. Importantly, our measurement is independent of the local distance ladder (LDL). Among individual late-universe probes, only the traditional LDL is more precise. We discuss our result in the context of the Hubble tension, the difference between $H_0$ measured in the late universe and the prediction based on early-universe probes such as the cosmic microwave background (CMB). We construct combinations of independent late-universe probes and show that the tension with the Planck CMB prediction is robust to excluding any one of the methods based on Type-Ia Supernovae, Cepheids, or the Tip of the Red Giant Branch. For example, we construct a 'no-SN' $H_0$ measurement, by replacing the DES-Dovekie constraint on $Ω_{\rm m}$ with that from DESI baryon acoustic oscillations, and then combining TDCOSMO-2026 with independent non-SN late-universe probes. This 'no-SN' late-universe probe is in 3.7$σ$ tension with Planck. Even after completely excluding the LDL, the tension with Planck persists at the 2.7$σ$ level.

titles.title: TDCOSMO 2026: new insights on the Hubble tension from strong lensing time delays

abstracts.value: We present BSMScanner, a framework in which a beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) parameter scan is specified as a set of declarative YAML documents rather than written as a program. The user declares the free parameters and their priors, the mass matrices and the diagonalisations that act on them, the observables, the theory-validity conditions and the likelihood terms. The framework validates this specification, resolves it into a dependency graph and compiles it once into a typed C++ evaluation kernel, which is then driven by an independently chosen scanning engine: uniform sampling, two differential-evolution engines, or a staged basin-discovery orchestrator, optionally followed by Markov-chain posterior refinement. Flavour physics matrix diagonalisation, PMNS and CKM construction in fixed conventions, tabulated oscillation likelihoods and a library of common flavour observables are provided by the framework and imported by name, so that a model file contains only model-specific definitions; quantities without a closed form, such as a relic density, enter through a C++ or Python plugin interface. We describe the specification schema, the observable and likelihood library, the scanning engines and their configuration, and demonstrate the framework on six benchmark models with $4$ to $26$ free parameters, giving for each the specification, the scan configuration, the resulting best fit and analytic cross-checks of the result.

titles.title: BSMScanner: a lightweight framework for beyond-the-Standard-Model global fits

abstracts.value: We propose a geometric realization of spacetime non-commutativity where the spacetime manifold remains smooth while the commutation relation between tangent and separation vectors of geodesic congruences is generalized via Frobenius' theorem. This non-commutative kinematic deformation leads to a modified Raychaudhuri equation with a shifted expansion scalar $\tilde θ=θ+θ^{\rm NC}$. We introduce a timelike and null-like Non-Commutative Energy Condition (NCEC) under which focusing and geodesic incompleteness can, in some regimes, persist even when the standard strong energy condition is violated. Using this, we generalize the key focusing lemmas, conjugate-point propositions, and singularity theorems for both timelike geodesics orthogonal to a Cauchy surface and null geodesics orthogonal to a trapped surface. Applied to a FLRW spacetime, we argue that $θ^{\rm NC}$ modifies both the Friedmann acceleration equation and the continuity equations. The non-commutative corrections separate into a universal modification of the dilution of the standard cosmological fluids and another contribution to the dark energy sector that is non-linear in energy density. Crucially, this provides a purely geometric origin for the evolution of dark energy, without introducing exotic dark energy fields or modifying Einstein's field equations.

titles.title: Non-Commutativity in Geodesic Congruences

abstracts.value: In this work, we study a theoretical scheme to investigate the monogamy of quantum steering in a hybrid exciton--cavity optomechanical (EOM) system. Within the Gaussian-state formalism, we quantify the steerability among the exciton, photon, and mechanical modes in both the steady-state and dynamical regimes. We establish and verify CKW-type monogamy inequalities for Gaussian steering and demonstrate that the distribution of bipartite steering among the three modes can be controlled through the system parameters. We further examine the influence of thermal noise and temporal evolution on the steering properties and the corresponding monogamy relations. Our results show that increasing the temperature generally suppresses the strength of Gaussian steering and modifies the degree of steering sharing imposed by the CKW-type monogamy relations. In contrast, in the dynamical regime, the steerability can increase with evolution time over suitable temporal windows, indicating that the transient dynamics can be exploited to enhance quantum correlations. These results highlight the potential of hybrid exciton--optomechanical platforms for controllable quantum correlations and provide a promising route toward the generation and manipulation of multipartite quantum resources.

titles.title: Monogamy of quantum steering in exciton--cavity optomechanical system

abstracts.value: Recently, the possibility of having sterile Majorana neutrinos charged under $B-L$ gauge symmetry in the bulk of the dark dimension has been explored. We point out a cosmological restriction on the Majorana mass of bulk neutrinos leading to mass $\gtrsim 100~{\rm GeV}$. This avoids the over-production of Kaluza-Klein neutrino towers in the early universe thus resolving the cosmological neutrino catastrophe of extra dimension scenarios. If the mass of the bulk neutrino is at the lower end of this bound, it can potentially also explain the recently observed Fermi halo excess on gamma rays through the evaporation of long-lived 5d (i.e. dark) black holes through Hawking radiation to bulk neutrinos, which promptly decay into standard model particles.
